basis: Defining fibrofolliculomas and pulmonary cysts; renal carcinoma is a separately diagnosed predisposed malignancy, despite its high frequency in the supplied series.
Protein O-glycosylation disorder causing muscular dystrophy. Ventilatory restriction in 2/4 reflects respiratory muscle dysfunction, without established intrinsic lung damage.
Defining mandibular, rib, scapular and chest-wall abnormalities with the cleft palate of Pierre Robin sequence.
Inherited loss of skin elasticity defines this heterogeneous group; pulmonary, vascular, skeletal and neurologic disease vary substantially by subtype.
Microcephaly and developmental impairment define the disease; scoliosis affects 4/7 (~57%). Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
A craniofacial bone fibro-osseous neoplasm; proximity to the sinuses or orbit does not establish additional organ damage.
Primary congenital microcephaly; associated short stature alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine disease.
Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation damages lung parenchyma. Atopic dermatitis is a separate associated disease; reactive eosinophilia does not establish a blood disorder.
Aplasia cutis with high myopia and retinal dysfunction defines the syndrome; calvarial skull defects occur in 80-99%.
Optic nerve inflammation with visual dysfunction is predominantly immune-mediated; toxic and nutritional forms within this umbrella are exceptions. Optic nerve maps to ocular.
Intellectual disability and seizures define the syndrome; cataract/glaucoma occur in 3/6 (50%) and cleft palate in 2/6 (33%). Small hands/feet alone do not establish skeletal damage.
Papillary urothelial carcinoma originates in the bladder or renal pelvis, both within the renal axis.
Inherited lipoprotein metabolism disorder with elevated HDL cholesterol; cardiovascular disease is not an intrinsic defining manifestation.
Keratinopathic ichthyosis with epidermal fragility and hyperkeratosis; no established common extracutaneous damage.
Defining arthrogryposis and craniosynostosis, microcephaly with cerebral abnormalities, and congenital cleft palate. Respiratory insufficiency does not establish intrinsic lung disease.
Eosinophil-mediated endomyocardial injury causes restrictive cardiomyopathy and mural thrombosis; associated hypereosinophilic or malignant disorders are separate conditions.
Cortical and cerebellar malformations cause developmental impairment and seizures; esotropia/deconjugate gaze reflect neurologic motor dysfunction without established intrinsic eye damage.
Malignant lymphoid-cell disease arising predominantly in the stomach; lymphoma also requires the immune mechanism axis.
Adenocarcinoma originates in esophageal mucosa; associated symptoms and risk factors do not establish other organ damage.
Lysosomal glycogen storage causes skeletal and respiratory muscle degeneration. Respiratory distress in 4/5 reflects muscle disease; elevated transaminases do not establish liver damage.
Benign tumor originates in mandibular bone; its location near the mouth does not establish gastrointestinal tissue involvement.
Pontocerebellar and motor-neuron disease; hearing and visual impairment each affect 9/11 (~82%), muscle atrophy 8/11 (~73%). Respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Developmental disability and seizures predominate; scoliosis is described as common, supporting approximately 30% or more. Palatal abnormalities vary across this duplication umbrella.
Bone fragility with osteopenia, recurrent fractures and deformity defines the disease. Blue sclerae in 1/8 neither meet frequency criteria nor establish visual damage.
Growth disorder with delayed skeletal maturation and clinodactyly in 30-79%. Hypoglycemia and developmental impairment are occasional; blue sclerae do not establish eye dysfunction.
